transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ames (Redwood AE), Sofia Reddy (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cobalt Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Platform), Elena Torres (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for PLG/self-serve adoption, criteria for hosted vs dedicated/private, security gating (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and next steps to run a short performance pilot. Customer wants clear latency/cost tradeoffs and a pathway from free credits to a small pilot.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits model
- Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) decision factors
- TTFT (time to first token) and integration work estimates
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
- Benchmarking plan, sample prompts, success metrics

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining on a tuesday afternoon i appreciate it i'm jordan on the ae side and with me is sofia our solutions engineer. quick check, can you each say hi and your role?
[00:08] Maya (Cobalt): hey jordan, maya here, head of ml at cobalt metrics. happy to be here.
[00:11] Ravi (Cobalt): ravi, platform engineering. we'll be doing the infra integration.
[00:13] Elena (Cobalt): elena, product, mainly overseeing the rollout and user metrics.
[00:16] Jordan: awesome. goal for today — understand your decision criteria for hosted vs dedicated/private and the time-to-first-token for a PLG onramp, plus figure out a small pilot.
[00:26] Maya: yeah our main thing is get something in prod quickly, we want self-serve for the product team but also need to know when we have to move to a dedicated/vpc setup for compliance. so TTFT and cost are big.
[00:36] Sofia (Redwood): totally. quick thing, our free credits quickstart usually gets teams to first request inside hours, often under a day for basic integration. TTFT depends mostly on auth, network rules, and whether you need a VPC/private control plane.
[00:51] Ravi: when you say hours, is that including SSO and network peering? because our environment has strict egress rules.
[00:58] Sofia: good call. no, when there's network peering or private endpoints it adds more time — typically a few days to set up VPC peering and routing and certs. hosted API with API key and standard IP allowlisting is the fastest path.
[01:12] Elena: so what's the delta in cost and latency between hosted and dedicated?
[01:16] Sofia: rough rule of thumb: hosted is cheapest to start because you pay per token and you benefit from shared optimizations like caching and batching across customers. dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p99 latency when you need consistent performance; cost becomes better at scale if you're doing sustained traffic.
[01:30] Jordan: and for private on-prem we charge a platform fee + support and you'll manage the infra; that's more for regulated customers.
[01:36] Ravi: do you support BYOK/KMS or HSM?
[01:39] Sofia: yes — we integrate with customer KMS providers, HSM is available for private deployments. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can arrange customer-managed keys with enterprise package.
[01:48] Maya: SOC 2? audit logs?
[01:50] Jordan: SOC 2 type II yes, we have audit logs, RBAC, SSO via SAML/SCIM; i'll send the security pack after the call.
[01:58] Elena: great. for TTFT our product team wants an end-to-end number: from signed up dev to hitting first token in our app. can you give an estimate?
[02:06] Sofia: for a PLG flow with free credits, typical path — sign up, API key, SDK drop-in (we have node/py), sample prompt set — many teams get first token in under 2 hours. if you need VPC/private link + SSO it becomes 2–5 business days depending on networking.
[02:22] Ravi: 2 hours sounds optimistic but reasonable for a demo. for integration we need specs for expected request headers, timeout, retry semantics. do you have docs?
[02:30] Jordan: yes docs.redwood.ai/quickstart link, i'll put the exact endpoint and sample curl in the follow-up.
[02:36] Maya: what's the difference between rounding behavior when you do batching and caching — like for embeddings vs chat? we have mixed workload.
[02:44] Sofia: embeddings are usually batched for cost efficiency; chat generation benefits from prefix kv caching. our runtime does continuous batching but respects latency SLOs; you can tune batch windows if you prefer lower latency at slightly higher cost. sometimes the transcript shows kv cache as key V cache, sorry that's a common transcription quirk.
[02:59] Maya: ha, okay. can you do quantized models in hosted?
[03:03] Sofia: yes, we host a set of quantized open models and have performance profiles in the model catalog. if you want a custom quantization or proprietary model we can do that in dedicated or private.
[03:13] Elena: what do you need from us to start a small pilot?
[03:16] Jordan: three things — 1) a set of ~50 representative prompts, 2) expected throughput (requests/min), and 3) security/compliance must-haves (do you need VPC, KMS, retention rules).
[03:26] Maya: we can provide prompts and throughput estimate. retention — we need logs for 90 days and ability to opt out of persistent storage for sensitive contexts.
[03:36] Sofia: we have retention controls and can disable transcript storage per route; we also support per-customer data isolation on dedicated.
[03:42] Ravi: on the network side we want a private link option. is that part of private only?
[03:46] Sofia: we offer private link and VPC peering for dedicated and private. hosted customers can do IP allowlisting and egress controls; but for fully private networking you go dedicated or private.
[03:56] Maya: in terms of SLA, what's typical p99 for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:59] Sofia: hosted p99 depends on model family; for small to mid-size models hosted p99 often under 600ms for many gen workloads, while dedicated configured with pinned GPUs can get p99 under 200–300ms. we can share model-specific perf profiles.
[04:13] Elena: sounds good. what about rollout strategies — can we canary to a cheaper model if the high-quality model fails?
[04:18] Jordan: yes, our console supports rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when latency/capacity constraints hit.
[04:25] Ravi: curious about pricing when you compare hosted unit cost vs reserved GPU pricing — do you have ballpark math?
[04:30] Jordan: we have a calculator i'll send. general pattern: hosted per-token is higher at scale; dedicated with reserved capacity amortizes GPU cost and reduces unit price for heavy steady usage.
[04:39] Maya: okay for our roadmap we want to start PLG hosted to get usage signal, then move to dedicated once we hit steady state. would that be a smooth migration?
[04:48] Sofia: yes we design model pinning and versioning to make migration straightforward — same API surface, you can change endpoint routing to a dedicated pool.
[04:55] Elena: what's the shortest runway to go from sign-up to an internal beta with 10 users?
[04:59] Sofia: with hosted and quickstart, you can be internal-beta-ready same day — provision API keys, add SDK to the front end, and run sample prompts.
[05:08] Jordan: let's talk specifics for the pilot — scope and success metrics.
[05:11] Maya: three metrics: 1) median latency < 400ms for our top 10 prompts, 2) cost per 1k requests under $X (we gave budgetary number in the RFP), 3) no data exfiltration and SOC2 compliance checks passed.
[05:24] Sofia: noted. for latency we can run a small benchmark against our hosted endpoints using your prompts to give real numbers. we typically do a 24–72 hour run that captures p50/p90/p99 and calorie — sorry i mean cost, not calorie.
[05:36] Ravi: (laughs) okay benchmarking is good. what does the engineer involvement look like on your side for a benchmark?
[05:41] Sofia: we'll run a mix: we provide a runbook, a script you can run, or we can run it from our infra if you share sample prompts and allowlist our IPs. usually 2–4 hours of engineering time to sanitize prompts and set up.
[05:53] Maya: okay. any red flags around data residency? some of our data must stay in eu regions.
[05:58] Jordan: we have regional hosting across NA and EU; you can pin region. private deployments can be fully on-prem for strict residency.
[06:06] Elena: role question — who will be our day-to-day contact?
[06:09] Jordan: i'll be your AE and primary contact for procurement; sofia will run the technicals and the benchmark.
[06:15] Ravi: timeline-wise we want a pilot starting early june, with a decision by end of june. is that feasible?
[06:20] Sofia: yes absolutely. pilot in early june, 2–3 week bench + small internal beta, then decision window end of june.
[06:28] Maya: ok good. any blockers we should know?
[06:30] Jordan: nothing on our side beyond getting your prompt set and the network folks doing allowlisting or peering if you want private link.
[06:37] Elena: procurement — do you have a standard pilot agreement or is it invoiced?
[06:41] Jordan: we have a simple TOU for free credits pilot; for paid pilots we draft an MSA/Scope. i can share a sample.
[06:49] Ravi: also curious about observability — can we get per-route token cost, per-model latency breakdown in the console?
[06:55] Sofia: yes console has token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, traces and auto alerting. we can add your route to a dashboard during pilot.
[07:05] Maya: good. one more product question: do you support function/tool calling or structured output? we have an extraction pipeline that expects JSON.
[07:12] Sofia: yes, function calling, tool invocation patterns and structured JSON outputs are supported; we have examples in the SDKs.
[07:19] Elena: sweet. any privacy features like redact on ingest?
[07:22] Sofia: we have on-ingest filters and rule-based redaction, plus the ability to opt out of persistent storage per route.
[07:30] Jordan: ok wrapping up, recap of next steps: jordan sends pricing & security pack; sofia schedules benchmark and prepares runbook; maya shares prompts and compliance matrix.
[07:40] Maya: i'll try to get prompts and the compliance items by friday.
[07:43] Ravi: i'll coordinate network allowlisting if needed.
[07:46] Jordan: perfect i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark slot and attach the doc links.
[07:52] Elena: thanks everyone.
[07:53] Jordan: thanks all, talk soon. bye.
